tasks.short: Research user needs and turn feedback into design requirements.

steps.what: Define research questions, participant criteria and methods in {DOCS}.
Recruit participants, explain participation terms and arrange sessions through {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Interview participants or observe usability sessions and record observations.
Combine research notes and existing feedback into an evidence pack in {DOCS}.
Group observations, inspect contradictions and describe themes in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved evidence pack with stable observation identifiers and unnecessary personal details removed.
loop.output: Draft themes, supporting observation identifiers, contradictions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate identifiers automatically; designer checks quotations, interpretation, minority experiences and unsupported generalisations.
loop.stop: One pass per bounded batch and one repair pass; unresolved or conflicting material goes to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can count labels but cannot reliably interpret varied descriptions of user difficulties.

steps.what: Translate findings into prioritised design requirements in {PROJECT}.
Agree which requirements enter the delivery backlog.

tasks.design: Configure recruitment and scheduling through {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, then assemble approved evidence from {DOCS} and {HELPDESK}. A bounded loop drafts traceable themes; the designer conducts sessions and interprets findings, while agreed requirements enter {PROJECT} after the manager's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling and evidence assembly crossed separate records. Interpreting observations required context that fixed labels could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features and small integrations handle coordination. Bounded text classification can prepare a traceable first synthesis.
tasks.still_hard: Recruiting a representative sample, observing behaviour and distinguishing stated preferences from actual needs remain demanding. GDPR requires a lawful basis, minimisation and suitable retention.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, ask useful follow-up questions and recognise when an apparent pattern reflects a biased sample.

ambition.what: Research participation for customers who use assistive technology.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into scheduling and assembling notes; more goes into observation and testing competing explanations. With agreed delegation, the designer can select follow-up studies within a research budget.

reach.task: Design participant sampling and distinguish segment differences from sampling noise.
reach.learn: Sampling methods, recruitment bias and the limits of qualitative evidence.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, evidence assembly and a bounded synthesis loop are feasible design patterns; research interpretation remains human.
Model-driven document metadata extraction exists, but outputs can be wrong; this supports reviewed extraction, not autonomous research conclusions.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results for this occupation.

assumptions: The company conducts project-based qualitative research and also receives customer feedback through the {HELPDESK}.
Existing participation records can govern permitted research use.
National rules may require employee consultation when staff participate or their behaviour is recorded.
The proposed use analyses design feedback without rating employees; EU AI Act obligations depend on the implemented use.
unknowns: Available recruitment channels, research budget and access needs of participants.
Lawful basis, recording permissions, retention periods and approved processing locations.
Whether national rules require works-council or employee consultation.
Whether the designer may commission follow-up studies.
research_questions: Can a pilot preserve contradictory observations and source traceability while reducing synthesis effort?
Which recruitment and scheduling features are already available in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}?
new_work: Check theme drafts against observations and retain minority findings.
Review free-text evidence for unnecessary personal information before model processing.
Maintain evidence identifiers, access permissions and retention rules.
Resolve failed invitations, integration errors and participant withdrawal requests.

tasks.short: Prepare, check and publish website updates.

steps.what: Receive website change requests through {EMAIL} and clarify missing details.
Decide scope, priority and delivery date in {PROJECT}.
Gather approved copy, images and destination links from {DOCS}.
Edit page content, assets and layout in the {CMS}.
Check preview content, responsive layouts, accessibility and essential interactions.
Approve the checked preview and publish or schedule it in the {CMS}.

tasks.design: Configure structured requests, reusable components, previews and publication approvals in {WORKFLOW} and {CMS}. A small integration retrieves approved material from {DOCS}; deterministic checks produce review evidence, and publication follows approval of the exact page version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived without complete material, and page preparation and checking depended on repeated manual work. Existing templates and approval features were often only partly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration can cover routine page changes, with small coded connectors and repeatable browser checks filling gaps. No model loop is needed for approved copy placed into known components.
tasks.still_hard: New interaction patterns, unusual layouts and content disputes still need design work. Automated accessibility checks cover only part of usability and accessibility.
tasks.human_edge: Judge visual hierarchy, reading order, interaction clarity and whether a change serves the page's purpose.

ambition.what: An approved-template event landing page service for event planners.

tasks.altitude: Routine publishing takes less of the week, leaving more time for reusable page patterns and difficult interactions. With agreed delegation, the designer can approve layout changes within established design standards.

reach.task: Prepare event landing pages and registration journeys.
reach.learn: Registration requirements, event deadlines and the information attendees need before booking.

evidence.claim: Structured content, reusable templates, versioned previews and publication approvals can handle routine website updates.
Playwright Test Agents can draft and repair browser tests; approved tests can then run deterministically.
Coding assistance exists, but the digest does not establish a 10-to-100-fold delivery improvement for this workflow.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for routine updates.

assumptions: Most updates change existing page types rather than introduce new application behaviour.
The {CMS} supports drafts, reusable components, version history and publication permissions.
The {OTHER} category in preview checking means browser and accessibility testing tools.
The design covers existing approved tracking; changes to personal-data collection require a separate GDPR assessment.
unknowns: Available {CMS} capabilities, interfaces and preview environment.
Proportion of changes requiring custom code or new page components.
Who approves factual claims, asset rights and publication.
Whether the change affects staff monitoring or requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which routine changes can existing {CMS} configuration handle without custom code?
Can approval be bound to an immutable preview version and invalidated after edits?
Which essential interactions need automated regression checks?
new_work: Maintain request fields, page templates and approved asset references.
Review preview differences and the accessibility issues that require human assessment.
Handle failed checks, stale approvals and publication exceptions.
Maintain browser checks as page components change.

tasks.short: Find broken website links, choose suitable destinations and maintain working references.

steps.what: Review link scans and observed inbound references using {OTHER} web crawling and analytics tools.
Reproduce failures with {OTHER} browser tools and distinguish temporary blocks from broken destinations.
Choose replacement destinations, redirects or removals using page context in the {CMS}.
Review proposed changes and apply approved link edits or redirects through the {CMS}.
Retest changed links with {OTHER} web crawling tools and record unresolved issues.
Ask external site owners through {EMAIL} to correct important inbound links.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled link scans with {OTHER} web crawling tools, then use deterministic retries and redirect checks to populate an exception queue in {PROJECT}. Approved changes are applied through {CMS}, retested and logged; templates in {EMAIL} prepare requests for external site owners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scanning could already be automated, but transient failures created noise and changes still required manual editing across pages. Destination choices depended on content context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scanners can be configured first. Small integrations can deduplicate failures, apply approved mappings and verify the result without a model.
tasks.still_hard: A successful response does not prove that a destination is relevant. External sites may block checks, hide references or ignore correction requests.
tasks.human_edge: Choose destinations that preserve meaning and user intent, and handle relationships with external site owners.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of broken links on active campaign landing pages.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated scanning and editing to a smaller exception queue and destination decisions. With agreed delegation, the designer can approve routine corrections within an established redirect policy.

reach.task: Prioritise link repairs and redirects by landing-page importance and search intent.
reach.learn: Redirect behaviour, canonical destinations and the limits of inbound-link data.

evidence.claim: Scheduled crawling, bounded retries, redirect validation and approved bulk edits are deterministic capabilities.
A link returning successfully can still be irrelevant; choosing an ambiguous replacement requires contextual judgement.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, with no documented job-specific saving in the digest.

assumptions: A mid-size marketing team uses periodic link scans, with manual reproduction and repair.
Observed inbound references come from available referral data and approved external-link reports; coverage is incomplete.
The {CMS} exposes link editing and redirect controls.
Aggregate referral data is sufficient; identifiable visitor records are unnecessary.
unknowns: Existing scanning features, scan coverage and access restrictions.
Who controls redirects and whether hosting changes need a separate technical owner.
Approved retry limits, crawl rate and publication permissions.
Which external relationships justify a correction request.
research_questions: How much of the current issue list consists of transient failures, blocked scans or duplicate reports?
Can the {CMS} apply and reverse approved changes while preserving version history?
Which landing pages justify faster checks than the rest of the site?
new_work: Maintain exclusions, retry rules and scan coverage.
Review ambiguous destinations and blocked checks.
Inspect failed edits, redirect loops and unsuccessful post-publication checks.
Maintain external contacts and follow up on important correction requests.

tasks.short: Prepare visual direction, storyboards and an agreed delivery timeline.

steps.what: Review the design brief, audience, deliverables and constraints in {DOCS}.
Find visual references and reusable assets in {DOCS} and {OTHER} design tools.
Create moodboards or storyboards and visual direction using {OTHER} design authoring tools.
Build a timeline with estimates, dependencies and review dates in {PROJECT}.
Discuss feasibility and negotiate scope, responsibilities and dates with the delivery team.
Approve the visual direction and delivery baseline before production starts.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator assembles reference sheets from tagged assets in {DOCS}, preserving provenance and usage restrictions. Configure reusable board layouts in {OTHER} design authoring tools and dependency templates in {PROJECT}; designers shape the concept, the team negotiates feasibility and the manager approves the baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assets, references and estimates were scattered, and each concept pack repeated assembly work. Creative direction and resource commitments could not be reduced to fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing authoring templates and project scheduling cover much of the preparation. Small coded generators can assemble consistent reference packs without generating new artwork.
tasks.still_hard: Original direction, coherent storytelling, asset rights and realistic capacity commitments remain difficult. A template can calculate dates only from credible estimates and dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: Develop a distinctive direction, explain its relationship to audience needs and negotiate a feasible creative scope.

ambition.what: Rapid concept packs for small event microsites.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into collecting references and laying out plans; more goes into visual exploration and delivery discussions. With an agreed budget boundary, the designer can select the initial concept direction for small projects.

reach.task: Develop a coherent visual direction across website and campaign materials.
reach.learn: Art direction, image licensing and translating brand principles into visual choices.

reach.task: Align a microsite production timeline with event announcements and registration deadlines.
reach.learn: Fixed event milestones, approval lead times and contingency planning.

evidence.claim: Tagged asset retrieval, reference-sheet generation and dependency templates can reduce preparation work without automating creative direction.
The digest provides no documented case establishing autonomous creative direction or reliable project estimates for this task.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for a reusable preparation toolkit.

assumptions: The company has reusable brand guidance, approved assets and recurring project types.
Asset tags and project templates are sufficient for a deterministic first implementation.
Capacity information is used for project planning rather than employee scoring.
GDPR applies to identifiable capacity data; national rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Quality of asset metadata and completeness of usage-rights records.
Available export features in the {OTHER} design authoring tools.
Reliability of capacity plans and historical project estimates.
Authority to select concepts or commit resources within a budget.
Whether access to staff capacity information requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which repeated assembly activities can existing authoring templates remove?
Do previous project timelines provide useful dependency templates without implying false precision?
Can reference packs preserve asset provenance through export and reuse?
new_work: Maintain asset tags, provenance and usage restrictions.
Refresh board layouts and project dependency templates.
Check suggested dates against actual availability and current scope.
Remove stale references and capture useful estimates after completed projects.

role.altitude: The role spends less time assembling material, repeating checks and transferring approved changes. More of the week goes into user observation, visual direction and difficult design choices; additional decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Work with a market research analyst on participant sampling and evidence quality.
Work with a search marketing strategist on destination relevance and repair priorities.
Work with a graphic designer on visual direction and asset rights.
Work with an event planner on landing pages and fixed delivery milestones.
skills_to_grow: Qualitative research and accessible participant recruitment.
Reusable content models and component-based page design.
Evidence traceability and privacy-conscious research handling.
Redirect policy, link diagnostics and search intent.
Art direction, dependency planning and scope negotiation.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small digital experience service that combines inclusive research, reusable event pages and rapid concept preparation. Use deterministic delivery and checking to make room for stronger design judgement and closer work with adjacent marketing roles.
